html:
The Battle of Mohács was fought on 29 August 1526 on the plain near Mohács in southern Hungary, where the army of Suleiman the Magnificent destroyed the army of the Kingdom of Hungary in a few hours.

The Hungarian army, led by the young King Louis II, was much smaller than the Ottoman one and attacked before all its forces had arrived. It was surrounded and crushed by Ottoman artillery and janissaries. Louis drowned in a stream as he fled, and many of the leading nobles and bishops died with him.

The battle ended medieval Hungary as an independent power. Suleiman sacked Buda and withdrew, and two kings were elected: the Hungarian noble John Zápolya and Ferdinand of Habsburg, Louis's brother-in-law. Their war drew the Ottomans back, to the first siege of Vienna in 1529 and the taking of Buda in 1541. Hungary was split into three for 150 years: Habsburg Royal Hungary in the north and west, Ottoman Hungary in the middle, and Transylvania under Ottoman protection.

For the Habsburgs it was a turning point. Ferdinand also inherited Bohemia, and these crowns became the base of the Austrian monarchy.
